scenario: AITA for expecting family time? | This morning I woke up and saw my husband watching video game streams, his typical pastime. Later he said the streamers he was watching were having cash giveaways that required participation to be entered. He continued to watch while he covertly built the kids' bikes in the garage as I had asked, then left to run a last-minute grocery errand for dinner, then came home and went upstairs to watch more streaming. After wrapping gifts, I did dishes and put dinner in the oven, and asked him to turn it off to spend time with me with/without kids. He said no. That the stream was only for today and it is not okay for me to expect him to stop doing what he finds enjoyable just because I want him to do something I find enjoyable. But if I was okay letting him spend $100 on app purchases for this game (same one he's watching) that he'd shut it off no problem. But last year he spent a little over $2,000 on in-app purchases for this game, and after a lengthy discussion, said he wouldn't buy anymore. So I'm not a huge fan of okaying any more money for it. It's almost 6pm and says he doesn't know when it will end, but that there are 2 more streamers left. I feel like the evening is almost over and I am so disappointed and feel saddened that he would rather watch games than spend time with me. Am I an asshole for being upset and having unrealistic expectations?

Scenario:
AITA for expecting family time? | This morning I woke up and saw my husband watching video game streams, his typical pastime. Later he said the streamers he was watching were having cash giveaways that required participation to be entered. He continued to watch while he covertly built the kids' bikes in the garage as I had asked, then left to run a last-minute grocery errand for dinner, then came home and went upstairs to watch more streaming. After wrapping gifts, I did dishes and put dinner in the oven, and asked him to turn it off to spend time with me with/without kids. He said no. That the stream was only for today and it is not okay for me to expect him to stop doing what he finds enjoyable just because I want him to do something I find enjoyable. But if I was okay letting him spend $100 on app purchases for this game (same one he's watching) that he'd shut it off no problem. But last year he spent a little over $2,000 on in-app purchases for this game, and after a lengthy discussion, said he wouldn't buy anymore. So I'm not a huge fan of okaying any more money for it. It's almost 6pm and says he doesn't know when it will end, but that there are 2 more streamers left. I feel like the evening is almost over and I am so disappointed and feel saddened that he would rather watch games than spend time with me. Am I an asshole for being upset and having unrealistic expectations?

Answer: <0 or 1>

Relationships thrive on mutual presence and collaboration, not just individual hobbies. - **His behavior is dismissive:** He frames her request as "unreasonable" while simultaneously using in-app purchases as leverage ("I’ll stop if you pay $100"). This reveals a pattern of prioritizing personal indulgence over partnership dynamics, especially given his history of $2,000 in-game spending last year. - **Context matters:** He *did* complete some tasks (building bikes, grocery run), but then returned to streaming while she handled dishes, dinner prep, and gift wrapping. Evening time is traditionally family time, and his refusal to disengage from a non-essential activity (streaming) during this period shows a lack of consideration for her emotional needs and shared responsibilities. - **No "asshole" here:** You’re not being unreasonable for wanting quality time with your partner. Healthy relationships require compromise, but this isn’t about "giving up" hobbies—it’s about mutual respect and shared priorities. His response (e.g., "I’ll only stop if you fund my game purchases") is the problematic behavior, not your request for connection. **Key takeaway:** This isn’t about "right or wrong" in a vacuum—it’s about whether his actions align with a partnership built on respect. His behavior suggests a deeper issue (e.g., boundary-setting, communication, or emotional availability), but *you* are not the asshole for wanting to spend time together. **建议:** Have a calm, non-confrontational conversation about *shared* expectations for evening routines. Focus on "we" language (e.g., "I feel disconnected when we don’t have time to talk after work—could we agree on a 30-minute screen-free window?"). If he consistently dismisses your needs, consider couples counseling to address underlying dynamics. 💬
